claim_verdicts.evidence: Definitional: the lesson introduces the term cache-stampede (glossary.yaml term cache-stampede, introduced_in backend.l2.cache-stampede). The mechanism it names is shown by claims 5 and 15.

ProductCache.cs@stage-2 l.18: `private static readonly TimeSpan Ttl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);` l.83: `StringSetAsync(key, json, Ttl)`. Lab run: right after cache-stampede.sh, `redis-cli TTL product:3` -> 281 (seconds, <= 300).

"When the call returns, the count on the semaphore is decremented. When a thread requests entry and the count is zero, the thread blocks. As threads release the semaphore by calling the ... SemaphoreSlim.Release method, blocked threads can enter." and "A lock with a count of 1 provides mutual exclusion ... Use SemaphoreSlim with a count of 1 instead". Note same page: "No guaranteed order ... governs which blocked thread enters the semaphore next."

"SemaphoreSlim provides a WaitAsync method that lets you await entry without blocking a thread"; "When the count is zero, WaitAsync enqueues a TaskCompletionSource and returns its task. Release either dequeues a waiter and completes it, or increments the count".

Code inspection ProductCache.cs@stage-2: without l.31-39, a miss after l.28-29 goes to l.41 `inner.FindAsync(id)` and l.42 `SetAsync` (only if product is not null), so N concurrent misses give N queries and N writes. Each such miss costs one GET (l.67 StringGetAsync) and one SET (l.82 StringSetAsync) on Redis on top of the query; with the lock, request 1 does two GETs. Matches 'a look and a write' in s6. Not executed (needs a code change).

Follows from claim 5 and l.28-29: once SetAsync (l.42) has stored the key, a new request's first GetAsync hits and returns before the lock, so the window is expiry/delete until the first SET. The query is the same single-row read whatever the value size (lab log round 1: `SELECT p.id, p.name, p.price_vnd FROM products AS p WHERE p.id = @p LIMIT 1`).

"This collection class is a thread-safe implementation. We recommend that you use it whenever multiple threads might be attempting to access the elements concurrently." GetOrAdd race: threadB's pair is added; "threadA performs a 'Get' and returns the data that was previously added by threadB" -> all callers get the one stored value, though "it is not guaranteed that the data that is returned by GetOrAdd is the same data that was created by the thread's valueFactory".

"In a try-finally statement, the finally block runs when control leaves the try block. Control might leave the try block as a result of normal execution, execution of a jump statement (that is, return, break, continue, or goto), or propagation of an exception out of the try block."

issues.quote: both get the same `SemaphoreSlim` for `product:3`, created the first time.
issues.text: 'created the first time' reads as 'created exactly once'. The docs say GetOrAdd's valueFactory runs outside the dictionary's lock, so two concurrent callers can each create a SemaphoreSlim; only one is stored and both get that one. The claim 9 ledger text is right; the prose adds a guarantee the docs do not give.
issues.fix: Replace 'created the first time.' with 'the one the dictionary stored first.'

issues.quote: two queries per expiry is exactly what the lesson says two copies give
issues.text: Explanation d (en and vi 'đúng là điều bài nói hai bản sẽ cho ra') overstates the lesson, which says 'up to two queries arrive' (s5) and 'can send two queries' (summary 5). Key a is still correct; only the explanation wording is too strong.
issues.fix: en d: replace 'exactly what the lesson says two copies give' with 'what the lesson says two copies can give, one per copy'. vi d: replace 'đúng là điều bài nói hai bản sẽ cho ra' with 'là điều bài nói hai bản có thể cho ra, mỗi bản một'.

issues.quote: so for a product that exists, and while Redis answers, one query per key is the limit.
issues.text: Round 2 adds two conditions without saying why they matter. 'A product that exists' I can rebuild from the code (a null product is not stored, so the next second look misses too). 'While Redis answers' I can only guess: the lesson never says what GetAsync returns when Redis fails. I am not stuck on the main idea, but I stop here.
issues.fix: Add a few words after each condition: 'for a product that exists (a missing one is never stored, so each waiter queries in turn)' and 'while Redis answers (if it fails, every second look misses)'; or drop the conditions.

issues.quote: because the lab's `docker-compose.yml` turns on its SQL command log for the `api` container
issues.text: 'The lab' appears nowhere else; I guess it is the example system that scripts/up.sh starts, but the lesson just replaced 'Compose' with scripts/up.sh and now names docker-compose.yml here without linking the two. The sentence also chains three clauses (what product_queries counts, who writes the log, why the log is on); I read it twice.
issues.fix: Replace 'the lab's `docker-compose.yml`' with 'the setup `scripts/up.sh` starts', and split the sentence after 'in the `api` container's log'.

issues.quote: On a miss, `inner` is the `EfProductRepository` that `ProductCache` holds, the object that sends the query.
issues.text: 'On a miss, inner is…' made me wonder whether inner is a different object on a hit. It is the same object; only its use is limited to the miss path.
issues.fix: Reword to: '`inner` is the `EfProductRepository` that `ProductCache` holds, the object that sends the query; it is only called on a miss.'
